# Lacuna v0.9.0

Lacuna `v0.9.0` is the migration and operational-hardening milestone. It does not add another
analytical method. It makes the released contracts easier to preserve, diagnose, measure, install,
and review before the project considers a stable `1.0` declaration.

## Highlights

- A published persisted-artifact compatibility manifest defines the current read boundary for
  `AnalysisResult` schema v1 (`0.1`-`0.9`), bundle v1 (`0.7`-`0.9`), and standardized audit profile
  v1 (`0.8`-`0.9`).
- The tagged-fixture corpus records exact SHA-256 and Git blob identities from prior releases.
  Regression tests prove that the retained result fixture is byte-identical across `v0.1.0` through
  `v0.8.0`, then validate and semantically round-trip every artifact through the current readers.
- `AuditProfile.from_dict(...)` / `from_json(...)` and standalone
  `BundleManifest.from_dict(...)` / `from_json(...)` provide strict, non-executing reads with
  fail-closed version, field, duplicate-key, non-finite, and nested-contract validation.
- `lacuna.diagnose_installation()` returns a versioned immutable health report with stable codes for
  package/distribution/native identity, Python and wheel support, dependency metadata, packaged
  schemas, and runtime configuration.
- `lacuna doctor --json --strict` is now an automation gate. Failures return nonzero by default;
  strict mode also rejects warnings. It reads no research data, performs no network or file writes,
  redacts configured paths, and never discovers or activates plugins.
- Benchmark artifact v5 adds one real integrated strategy workload spanning forward labels, signal
  IC, purged K-fold, stationary bootstrap, cost stress, point-in-time joins, vendor/backtest
  adapters, and standardized-audit composition. Repeated output checksums and traced memory are
  enforced.
- The initial v5 profile found the declared cost surface and point-in-time join dominate the smoke
  workload, with no accidental repeated cross-phase call. Production semantics remain unchanged
  instead of adding an unevidenced optimization.
- A complete Python API surface and versioned reference-coverage manifest enumerate all 65 root
  exports and 18 supported submodules. Contract tests require implementation exports, cumulative
  API fixtures, human symbol sections, and semantic design routes to agree exactly.

## Compatibility and trust boundary

Core `0.9.0` is additive over every published `0.1.x` through `0.8.x` Python contract. Persisted
format versions remain independent of the package version: current identity migrations validate
the existing format rather than silently rewriting it. Strict standalone manifest parsing does not
replace full `.lacuna` archive verification.

Diagnostic `PASS` means the installed runtime contract is healthy; it does not certify a research
result. Bundle digest verification establishes integrity, not publisher authenticity. Benchmark
timings are environment evidence, not universal latency promises. Adapter declarations still
remain caller-supplied evidence rather than vendor or methodology certification.

The separately versioned options extension advances to `0.1.3` only to expand its compatible core
range to `lacuna>=0.5,<0.10`. Its exact `0.1.x` exports, signatures, and analytical semantics are
unchanged and rerun through property, coverage, profile-integration, packaging, and clean joint-
installation gates.

## Distribution

This release is distributed through GitHub because the `lacuna` name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated
project. The release contains four target-smoke-tested CPython 3.11 stable-ABI core wheels, one
universal options wheel, both source distributions, `SHA256SUMS`, and GitHub provenance for every
distribution. Each core wheel must pass the strict installation diagnostic gate on its target.

The v1 readiness audit finds no remaining internal implementation row. `1.0.0` is still blocked by
the technical specification's explicit requirement for real users applying Lacuna to independent
research stacks. No independent testers were available for `0.9`, so this release makes no such
claim and does not convert maintainer/CI evidence into external validation.
